source_ref: osf.io/4b85w data paper/codebooks/processed_data_dictionary.csv (Variable, Section Header, Field_Type, Field_Label, possible values) -- Oxford ARC study; Parsons, Todorovic, Lim, Songco & Fox (2022) data and protocol paper
note: Level-1 source with no mapping inference at all. The Oxford ARC data paper ships codebooks/processed_data_dictionary.csv, one row per variable, and all 44 live item codes appear in its Variable column verbatim; item_text is that row's Field_Label, section_prompt its Section Header. The codes are self-describing besides (activity_exercise_outside, media_why_tv_news), so a permutation could not survive a reading. The table pools two response formats and the dictionary distinguishes them by Field_Type, which is why option_text is populated for some items and not others: 36 'radio' items carry the labels '1, Never | 2, Rarely | 3, Sometimes | 4, Often | 5, Always' and ship all five; the 8 'text' items are average hours per day, a free numeric quantity rather than a category, so their levels 0-5 are hours and carry no option label. That gives 180 labelled option cells and 48 deliberately blank. Two sections are carried: the hours block under 'Please report the average number of hours per day...' and the reasons block under 'please rate how much you did this activity for the following reasons'. instructions is empty because the dictionary gives no whole-table framing distinct from those two section headers. audit_batch.R WARNs on this table and both halves are the instrument, not a defect: the 36 reason items fall into six clusters of six with near-identical n inside each (2,264-2,304 up to 6,193-6,277) because each medium's six reasons were shown only to respondents who used that medium, and the blank-option_text half is the hours-per-day format described above.
public_note: 44 items on two response formats. The 36 reason items run 1 = Never to 5 = Always. The 8 remaining items ask for average hours per day, so their 0-5 values are hours rather than scale points and carry no option labels.

note: The three additional questions are reproduced verbatim in the article's S1 File under 'Part 4 : Additional questions', followed by 'Participants gave a single answer to each item.' Two of the three codes match their question on content: addreasontochooserehab against 'Why did you choose to study a therapy programme', and addmyviewondevelopmentinrehab against 'My personal views on the prospect of rehabilitation industry in China'. THE THIRD IS ASSIGNED BY ELIMINATION and the content does not corroborate it: addcompetitioninreha reads 'competition' while the remaining question is 'To what degree does the pressure of your current studies affect your career plan.' -- plausible if the code glosses competitive study and job-market pressure, but not established. That item also uses resp levels 1-4 where the other two use 1-5, and the S1 File states no response options for any of the three, so the difference is unexplained and option_text is empty throughout. The questionnaire was administered in Mandarin (the article excludes students unable to read or write it) but the supplement carries the English only -- zero CJK characters across all three supporting files -- so the base fields hold English by the recorded fallback. language is not set because the wording shipped is the study's own English rendering of its own instrument rather than a substitute for an original the deposit withholds; flagging for the #1777 backfill either way.
public_note: Three single-answer questions on career choices, transcribed from the article's S1 File. Two are matched to their item code on content; the third, addcompetitioninreha, is assigned by elimination and its code does not obviously describe the question it carries, so treat that one item's wording as provisional. No response options are published for any of the three, and one uses four levels where the others use five.

source_ref: Gratz & Roemer (2004), 'Multidimensional Assessment of Emotion Regulation and Dysregulation', J Psychopathol Behav Assess 26:41-54, Table III (all 36 items) and p.44 (response anchors); item codes and used resp levels from the live table; DERS_SUM_POST from the deposit, osf.io/9jgxs 'amps psychometric eval.csv'. Study paper: 10.1007/s12671-023-02144-1 (PMC12959836).
note: Wording is the instrument's own publication; the mapping is reconstructed and verified on three routes (see verify_paampsmartsud_saba_2023_ders.R). THE NUMBERING TRAP: Table III numbers items in the original 41-item pool, not the published 36-item numbering the deposit uses. Pool items 2, 11, 13, 18 and 36 were dropped and the survivors renumbered 1..36 in ascending order; shipping Table III's numbers as-is would have misassigned most of the scale. That renumbering is what was tested: it places the article's 11 reverse-scored items on exactly positions 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 10, 17, 20, 22, 24, 34, which the deposit's own DERS_SUM_POST independently pins (dropping DERS_37_POST and reversing those 11 reproduces the total for all 90 complete rows, where no other single-column drop exceeds 42 of 90 and no-reverse scoring matches 6). DERS_37_POST is therefore NOT a scored DERS item and its wording is unknown, so it ships with empty item_text and empty option_text rather than being guessed; its resp rows are present so the item and resp sets still match the live table. DEVIATIONS: two PDF rendering artefacts were normalised in the text -- the fi/fl ligatures (U+FB01/U+FB02) to ASCII, and the typographic apostrophe (U+2019) to "'" -- neither is a feature of the administered form. Response anchors are Gratz & Roemer's own, including their percentage bands; note that the study paper renders the low anchor as 'never' where the instrument's publication says 'almost never (0-10%)', and the instrument was followed. No administered instruction text was recovered from either the deposit or the two papers, so instructions and section_prompt are empty; the study describes a 30-day reporting window and Gratz & Roemer describe the task as indicating 'how often the items apply to themselves', but neither reproduces what respondents were shown. RIGHTS: cleared under the corrected test settled in #1945 -- the DERS carries no licence fee and no quotable no-redistribution clause (APA PsycTests 10.1037/t01029-000 is behind SSO and could not be quoted either way), so silence is permission. Supersedes this table's earlier blocked note, which was held partly on the superseded stricter reading. On DERS_37_POST specifically: it is not identifiable, but it does sit in the same administered matrix -- n = 180 responses and an observed range of 1-5, identical to all 36 scored items, with mean 1.86. That is why its resp rows are kept; the option labels are still left blank rather than inferred from the block, since an unidentified item could carry its own anchors.
public_note: The 36-item Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale administered post-intervention. resp runs 1-5 over Gratz & Roemer's anchors, stored RAW -- the 11 reverse-keyed items (DERS_1, _2, _6, _7, _8, _10, _17, _20, _22, _24, _34_POST) are not pre-reversed, so reverse them before summing. DERS_37_POST is in the response table but is not a scored DERS item and its wording is not recorded anywhere in the deposit or the papers; it ships with no item text rather than a guess. Its observed responses do span 1-5 with the same respondent count as the scored items, so it appears to have been administered on the same grid.

source_ref: Deposit SPSS file 'Data_main experiment_13 countries_July 2 2024.sav' (the file behind the dictionary's OSF view_only link, supplied directly), variable labels NFC_1-NFC_5 and their value labels; data/pezzuti_2025_coolpeople.do for the code derivation. Article: Pezzuti, Warren & Chen (2025), 'Cool People', J Exp Psychol Gen, 10.1037/xge0001799.
note: Level-1 extraction, no mapping inference. The .sav carries a variable label per item, and data/pezzuti_2025_coolpeople.do does `rename *, lower` and then `gen item = "`var'"`, so the live code nfc_1-nfc_5 IS the lowercased source column name. Each label is a shared stem plus the item, split on ' - ': the stem became section_prompt and the remainder item_text. CORRECTS THIS TABLE'S EARLIER BLOCKED NOTE, which called the five items a Need for Cognition short form -- that was a guess from the code name and it is wrong. The items are about rules, instructions and standardized work procedures. They are the uncertainty-avoidance dimension of the CVSCALE: the article states that in the initial samples it 'included items to measure beliefs about cultural dimensions' citing Yoo et al. (2011), and all five wordings match CVSCALE's uncertainty-avoidance items. That identification comes from the citation plus the wording match, NOT from any source that keys these codes to a named dimension, and the study's own materials never name it -- they only label the block NFC. Note also that CVSCALE is normally administered on 5 points and this study used 7. ANCHORS: the .sav value labels read 'strongly disagree1' and 'strongly agree7' -- Qualtrics appended the scale number, which was stripped. Points 2-6 carry no label in the source and are left blank rather than padded with their own number. The typographic apostrophe in item 1 was normalised to ASCII. COVERAGE: only 844 of the 3,972 respondents in the live table answered this block, which matches the article -- these were exploratory measures run only in the initial samples. RIGHTS: clears the corrected test in #1945. No fee or no-redistribution clause is quotable for the CVSCALE. The article PDF does carry an APA notice that it 'is not to be disseminated broadly', but that governs the article, not the instrument, and no wording here was taken from the article -- it all comes from the study's own .sav.
public_note: Five uncertainty-avoidance items, answered on a 7-point agree/disagree scale whose endpoints alone were labelled in the source. Only 844 of the 3,972 respondents saw this block: it was an exploratory measure administered in the initial samples only, so most ids have no response. The item codes read 'nfc' but the items are not a Need for Cognition measure.

source_ref: ResearchBox #2404, researchbox.org/2404, 'Identity as a Resource or a Demand' -- Data/IRS1.sav and Data/IRS 2.sav variable and value labels, cross-read against the box's own generated Codebook/IRS1.sav___CODEBOOK.csv and Codebook/IRS 2.sav___CODEBOOK.csv; data/singh_2025_identity.do for the code derivation. Article: 10.1371/journal.pone.0318449 (CC-BY), which reproduces item 3 as its sample item.
note: Level 1 with the mapping stated by the source rather than inferred: each .sav variable label opens with the item's own number, and those numbers run 1-11 matching PBA1-PBA11 exactly. Label format is '<n>  <item text>:<stem>', so the stem became section_prompt and the remainder item_text; both studies' labels were parsed independently and assert-checked to agree on all 11 wordings and the stem. The live lowercase codes come from data/singh_2025_identity.do's `rename *, lower`. Item 3 matches the article's sample item, 'I avoid spending leisure time with members of other ethnic/racial groups', which is an independent check on the mapping. THE LIVE TABLE POOLS BOTH STUDIES: IRS1.sav N=618 and IRS 2.sav N=852 sum to the 1,470 live ids, and cov_study marks which. That matters for the anchors, because the two administrations labelled the scale differently: study 1 used 'Neither agree nor disagree' at point 3 and 'Strongly agree' at 5, study 2 used 'Neutral' and 'Strongly Agree'. Points 1, 2 and 4 are identical in both. Itemtext allows one row per (item, resp), so only one rendering could ship; study 1's fuller standard Likert wording was used, and study 2's variants are recorded here. A user who needs the exact administered midpoint label can split on cov_study. UNBLOCKING: the dictionary URL for this table is a box link carrying a peer-review passcode and was not reachable; ResearchBox #2404 was supplied directly and is public. Per the user's ruling the dictionary URL is being left as it is -- it opens in a browser and editing it would affect other documents -- so this provenance row is the pointer to the reachable source. RIGHTS: clears the corrected test in #1945. The article is CC-BY and no fee or no-redistribution clause is quotable for the Behavioral Avoidance Scale.
public_note: Eleven behavioral-avoidance items adapted to ethnic/racial groups, answered 1 (Strongly disagree) to 5 (Strongly agree). The table pools the paper's two studies -- see cov_study. The two studies rendered the midpoint differently ('Neither agree nor disagree' in study 1, 'Neutral' in study 2); the shipped option_text uses study 1's wording throughout, so the point-3 and point-5 labels are exact for study 1 and differ cosmetically for study 2.
